character.name: Lev Davidovich Trotsky (Leon Trotsky)
character.role: Bolshevik Central Committee member; deputy of the Petrograd Soviet, just released from Kresty on bail

liabilities.name: Arrogance
liabilities.description: On any failed Cunning or Presence check involving a named rival, automatically add 1 enmity pip (enforced by the application, not GM discretion).

liabilities.name: Visible Target
liabilities.description: Antisemitic opponents gain an edge on attempts to discredit the character in certain constituencies - the GM should reflect this in narrative framing and DC-setting when relevant, not as an automatic numeric trigger.

flags.party_position: Central Committee member (elected in absentia at the Sixth Congress, August 1917)

lenin.note: Allies since the summer, when Trotsky's group joined the Bolsheviks. Lenin is in hiding in Finland and reaches you only by letter.

kamenev.note: Leads the Bolshevik fraction in the Soviet. Old acquaintance; more cautious than you, and he thinks the Soviet majority should be used to build a socialist coalition, not to rise.

zinoviev.note: In hiding since July, close to Lenin personally but closer to Kamenev politically. Wary of you.

stalin.note: Edits the party paper. Correct but cold.

kollontai.note: Arrested after the July Days too. A real ally.

joffe.note: Old comrade from your own group. The person you trust most in politics.

martov.note: Menshevik-Internationalist leader and an old friend from the Iskra days. He shares half your critique and none of your conclusions.

dan.note: Fyodor Dan, Menshevik leader on the Soviet presidium. Sees you as the man who will wreck the Soviet.

kerensky.note: Minister-President. His government put you in prison.

dan.note: Opposes you on every question before the Soviet.

kerensky.note: His ministry is still pressing the July charges against you.

bail_conditions.description: Released on bail pending trial on the July charges (incitement, and the 'German agent' accusation)

factions.name: Bolsheviks
factions.note: Swelling since Kornilov. Kamenev leads the fraction and wants to use the majority carefully; the district organizers want to use it now.

factions.name: Non-party soldiers' delegates
factions.note: Elected by regimental committees. Angry about the front and the officers, wary of any party - will follow whoever talks about peace and bread.

factions.name: Left Socialist-Revolutionaries
factions.note: Breaking from the SR leadership over land and the war. Natural allies, but they want to be partners, not followers.

factions.name: Menshevik-Internationalists
factions.note: Martov's people. Agree with much of the critique, fear a one-party seizure. Persuadable by argument, not by pressure.

factions.name: Socialist-Revolutionaries (leadership)
factions.note: Chernov's and Avksentiev's party machine, still tied to coalition with the government.

factions.name: Mensheviks (defensist)
factions.note: Chkheidze, Tsereteli and Dan's bloc - the old presidium. They built this Soviet and believe it must not become a Bolshevik instrument.

data.loyalty_scale: +3 marches for the Soviet unprompted · +2 fights for the Soviet when called · +1/0/-1 stays in barracks · -2 fights for the Provisional Government when ordered · -3 moves against the Soviet unprompted

units.name: Red Guards
units.note: Factory militias, rifles handed out during the Kornilov scare. Enthusiastic, badly trained, short of officers.

units.name: Kronstadt sailors
units.note: Baltic Fleet sailors from the island base - the most radical armed men in Russia. A day's movement from the city.

units.name: Pavlovsky Regiment
units.note: Its committee is solidly Bolshevik. Barracks on the Field of Mars, a few hundred meters from the Winter Palace.

units.name: Keksgolmsky Regiment
units.note: Radicalized, close to the Bolshevik Military Organization.

units.name: Volynsky Regiment
units.note: Mutinied first in February and is proud of it. Sympathetic, but won't move without a reason.

units.name: Litovsky Regiment
units.note: Joined the February rising early. Leans left; tired.

units.name: Izmailovsky Regiment
units.note: Soviet-leaning, committee divided between Bolsheviks and SRs.

units.name: Grenadier Regiment
units.note: On the Petrograd side, near the Bolshevik district committees.

units.name: Finlyandsky Regiment
units.note: On Vasilievsky Island. Sympathetic, not committed.

units.name: Moskovsky Regiment
units.note: Vyborg side, surrounded by the most militant factories in the city.

units.name: Egersky Regiment
units.note: Undecided. Its officers still have some hold over it.

units.name: Preobrazhensky Regiment
units.note: The oldest Guards regiment. Wants no part of a fight between socialists.

units.name: Semyonovsky Regiment
units.note: Crushed the Moscow rising in 1905 and hasn't forgotten it; neither have the workers. Neutral, watchful.

units.name: Peter and Paul Fortress garrison
units.note: Holds the fortress and its arsenal - tens of thousands of rifles - with guns facing the Winter Palace across the Neva. Wary of the Bolsheviks.

units.name: Don Cossack regiments (1st, 4th, 14th)
units.note: Experienced cavalry. Distrust the Soviet, but bitter at Kerensky for how he treated Kornilov. Their neutrality is for sale; their loyalty isn't.

units.name: Officer cadets (junkers)
units.note: Students of the military schools - young, disciplined, and the government's most reliable armed men in the city.

units.name: 1st Petrograd Women's Battalion
units.note: Volunteers raised to shame the army into fighting on. Loyal to the government, quartered outside the city at Levashovo.

units.name: Armored car units
units.note: A few dozen machine-gun cars. Whoever has them controls the streets for an afternoon - their committee hasn't chosen.

units.name: Latvian Rifle regiments (12th Army)
units.note: The best-disciplined troops on the Northern Front, and the most Bolshevik. Held the line before Riga.

units.name: 5th Army (Dvinsk)
units.note: Huge, war-weary front army; its committees are drifting left. Strength is the men who'd move, not the rolls.

units.name: 3rd Cavalry Corps (Krasnov)
units.note: Kornilov's spearhead in August, pulled back to Ostrov and Pskov under General Krasnov. The government's nearest loyal cavalry.

units.name: Caucasian Native Cavalry Division
units.note: The 'Savage Division' - Kornilov sent it on Petrograd; Muslim agitators talked it out of the attack. Sullen and unreliable.

units.name: Baltic Fleet crews (Helsingfors)
units.note: Centrobalt is under Bolshevik influence (Dybenko). Battleships and destroyers at Helsingfors; a few days from the Neva.

units.name: Stavka garrison (Mogilev)
units.note: Guards supreme headquarters. Obeys the commander-in-chief, whoever that is this week.

units.name: Tekke Cavalry Regiment (Kornilov's guard)
units.note: Turkmen horsemen personally loyal to Kornilov, guarding him and his generals at Bykhov.

units.name: Minsk garrison and Western Front reserves
units.note: The Minsk Soviet leans Bolshevik; the front headquarters does not.

units.name: 1st Polish Corps (Dowbor-Musnicki)
units.note: Polish units being gathered into a corps. Answers to Polish politics, not Russian; distrusts the Bolsheviks.

units.name: Czechoslovak Corps
units.note: Czech and Slovak volunteers and ex-prisoners, well officered, meaning to fight Austria. Neutral in Russian quarrels - for now.

units.name: Ukrainianized units (Central Rada)
units.note: Regiments that have declared for the Kiev Rada. Fight for Ukraine, not for either side in Petrograd.

units.name: Moscow garrison (reserve regiments)
units.note: Tens of thousands on the rolls; slow to move either way.

units.name: Moscow Red Guards
units.note: Factory militias from Zamoskvorechye and the outer districts.

units.name: Moscow officer cadets (Alexandrovsky and ensign schools)
units.note: Will fight for the government in Moscow, and did.

units.name: Don Cossack Host (Ataman Kaledin)
units.note: Kaledin's Cossacks at Novocherkassk. Will fight for the Don; uncertain beyond it.

units.name: Kuban Cossack Host
units.note: The Kuban Rada guards its own autonomy.

units.name: Orenburg Cossacks (Dutov)
units.note: Ataman Dutov's men, astride the road to Turkestan.

units.name: Donbass and Kharkov Red Guards
units.note: Miners and railwaymen of the Donets basin.

units.name: Tsaritsyn garrison
units.note: 'Red Tsaritsyn' - the garrison sided with the Bolsheviks early.

units.name: Kazan garrison
units.note: A large reserve garrison on the Volga; the State Bank's gold is in the city.

units.name: Urals factory militias
units.note: Armed workers of the Ekaterinburg and Perm works.
